chapter: Beginnings and early New Orleans scene
title: Musicians in the family and the Ninth Ward players
summary: Only a guitar-playing relative of his mother's played in the family; Allen asks about Ninth Ward musicians, and Williams says they came up later than he did.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I don't know. Did you have any musicians in your family? Or did your mother sing or anything like that?

No, it wasn't. One was a, he was a guitar player. And that was Reverend Griffin's brother, Kenderman, you know, my mother. He was a guitar player. What was his name? Nah, I can't think of his name now. He did so long, man.

Was he down in the Ninth Ward? Huh? Yeah. He down in the Ninth Ward? Yeah, Ninth Ward, yeah. Did you know Ambrose and Henry Ford and those guys and Freddie Gould and all those guys down in the Ninth Ward? Yeah, yeah. Were they playing when you were young?

Freddie Gould and them? When you were a kid, yeah. Well they, I don't know if they, they didn't, they wasn't, you know what I mean? They come up way after in the time, you know what I mean? Playing, you know? They come up way after. But the old man was.
Yeah. They father. Yeah, he was playing. Man, them boys come up way behind, you know? Yeah, they come way after.
